key_insight: The 3D/2D perovskite interface band alignment is highly sensitive to surface termination and composition, meaning chemical details can strongly reshape device energetics.
engineering_relevance: For perovskite solar cell design, 2D passivation layers must be chosen and interfaced carefully because they can improve stability while also changing work function and charge transfer barriers.
method: Computed work function, electron affinity, and band offsets across interfaces
evidence_signal: The abstract reports termination-dependent valence band offsets of about 0.2–0.7 eV and conduction offsets around 0.25 eV, along with strong work-function variation and interfacial potential slopes.
watch_item: These are preliminary simulation results, so the predicted offsets should be validated against experimental interfaces and real microstructural variability.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
